brief: DESIGN A: young adult male trail athlete, wiry athletic build, short windswept auburn hair with distinctive forelock, expressive determined eyes, dark-teal sleeveless technical vest with ivory collar and coral scarf tucked back, charcoal tapered running trousers, detailed tan trail shoes and wrist wraps. A relaxed three-quarter ready-to-move stance: forward knee slightly bent, back leg bearing weight, one open hand extended at waist level and the other holding a short rolled training towel near shoulder. Make his personality energetic and approachable. Draw the towel and hand unambiguously.
prompt: Create ONE ORIGINAL full-body human battle trainer sprite for a high-quality GBA-era monster-battle fitness RPG. This must be hand-crafted-looking PIXEL ART in the visual language of 2000s Japanese handheld trainer battle sprites, not a geometric avatar, not chibi, not a painting with a pixel filter. Aim for a logical 64 by 64 pixel grid: at a larger output resolution each logical pixel should be a uniform square block. Fine readable face with eyebrows, natural human anatomy about 5.5 heads tall, articulated knees/elbows/hands, weight carried plausibly, dynamic asymmetric pose. Detailed clothing through carefully shaped pixel clusters, folds and seams; small tonal ramps (3-4 shades per material); deliberate single-logical-pixel selective dark colored outline. Upper-left light, coherent shadows on right and under chin/folds. Entire head, hands and feet in frame, centered, approximately 56 logical pixels tall with transparent margins. Eye-level three-quarter battle presentation, no ground, no oval shadow, no scenery, no words, no labels, no checkerboard painted into image. Genuine transparent RGBA background. Color palette navy ink, warm skin highlights, ivory and an individual accent color. Avoid blocky rectangle limbs, huge head, thick black outlines, flat clothing, excessive tiny multicolor noise, airbrush, blur, gradients and fake scanlines. No copied franchise characters, trademark symbols, balls or logos. Deliver a single sprite, not multiple views or a sheet.
